why: phase-515 R10 stage 1b (2026-10-27): the executor's node-id-keyed parameter forms left the Rust user surface (behind the sealed `nros_node::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi`, as R9 stage 1 did for the C-shaped entry points), so the node is the one user-facing parameter receiver, as rclrs's is. `Node::for_each_argv_param_override` forwards to `Executor::for_each_argv_param_override_on(node_id, ...)`; the store is still the executor's one table (phase-426 W1). The visitor form of `rust:Node::argv_param_overrides`. PRIOR ROW (`rust:Executor::for_each_argv_param_override_on`): issue 2104 -- the visitor form of `rust:Executor::argv_param_overrides_on`, with the same selection (last override of a name wins, a `node:` override applies only to that node, typed bool, integer, double, then string). It hands each override to a callback by reference instead of collecting them into a `Vec`, because a `ParameterValue` holds inline buffers of about 8 KiB and collecting cost one value per override on the caller's stack; the C++ shim's `get_parameter_overrides()` forwards to it. Upstream returns the overrides as a map from the node's own `NodeParameters`; ours live in the executor's one parameter store, so the node is an ARGUMENT, as for the collecting reader. Test: `packages/core/nros-node/src/executor/tests.rs` (`the_node_carries_the_whole_parameter_surface`).
